papers.title: The Potential of AI-Driven High-Content Imaging in Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: We have authored a compelling and timely review that highlights the transformative potential of high-content imaging for discovering small molecules (SMs). SMs are crucial for advancing drug potency, selectivity, and precision, and their assessment through specialized cellular assays accelerates drug development. High-content imaging (HCI), which seamlessly integrates automated microscopy with sophisticated image analysis powered by artificial intelligence (AI), is revolutionizing cell-based assays by enabling a comprehensive evaluation of cellular parameters following drug treatment. The rich
papers.summary: This review highlights how AI-powered high-content imaging (HCI) is transforming drug discovery by enabling comprehensive, automated analysis of cellular responses to small molecules. The authors emphasize that integrating automated microscopy with AI-based image analysis accelerates the evaluation of drug potency, selectivity, and precision, thereby speeding up the development of new therapeutics.

papers.title: FDA-Approved Drug Repurposing as p53 Mutants Rescue Candidates Using Structure-Based Virtual Screening and Molecular Simulations.
papers.abstract: The restoration of mutant p53 stability is a highly sought-after strategy in targeted cancer therapy. This study presents a structure-based virtual screening and molecular dynamics approach to nominate FDA-approved drugs as candidate stabilizers of mutant p53 for downstream experimental validation. A virtual screening library of FDA-approved compounds was docked against three representative p53 mutants (7DHY, 7DHZ, and 7V97) to evaluate their binding potential. The prioritized candidates demonstrated consistent, multi-conformer binding affinities. Protein-ligand interaction profiling revealed
papers.summary: This study uses structure-based virtual screening and molecular dynamics to identify FDA-approved drugs that could stabilize mutant p53, a key target in cancer therapy. The authors docked a library of approved compounds against three p53 mutants and prioritized candidates with consistent binding affinities and favorable interaction profiles, providing a shortlist for experimental validation.

papers.title: SurroDock: A Deep Learning Surrogate for Accelerated Pre-Docking Ligand Prioritization in Structure-Based Virtual Screening.
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of make-on-demand and public chemical libraries has made exhaustive docking-based structure-based virtual screening increasingly difficult. This study introduces SurroDock, a lightweight deep-learning surrogate designed to approximate AutoDock Vina docking scores from low-cost two-dimensional molecular features, serving as a practical pre-filter for docking. SurroDock was evaluated for estrogen receptor alpha using two distinct conformations: an agonist-bound (PDB ID: 1GWR) and an antagonist/SERM-bound (PDB ID: 3ERT). The dataset comprised approximately 334,000 unique compo
papers.summary: SurroDock is a lightweight deep-learning surrogate that predicts AutoDock Vina docking scores from 2D molecular features, enabling rapid pre-filtering of large chemical libraries before exhaustive docking. Tested on estrogen receptor alpha with two conformations and ~334,000 compounds, it offers a practical acceleration strategy for structure-based virtual screening.

papers.title: Deciphering the Leading-Edge Spatiotemporal Microenvironment of Hepatocellular Carcinoma for Targeted Drug Discovery Using SpaPred.
papers.abstract: The leading-edge (LE) of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a critical region driving malignant progression and is closely associated with high patient mortality and marked intratumoral heterogeneity. Multi-omics integration identified elevated expression of SPARC and IGFBP7 in the LE region, which was associated with stromal remodeling-related transcriptional programs and an immune-depleted microenvironment. Cell-cell communication and pathway analyses further suggested potential links between LE-associated stromal states and pro-invasive signaling programs. Furthermore, we developed SpaPred,
papers.summary: This study characterizes the leading-edge (LE) microenvironment of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) using multi-omics data, identifying elevated SPARC and IGFBP7 expression linked to stromal remodeling and immune depletion. The authors developed SpaPred, a predictive tool for targeted drug discovery in this aggressive tumor region.

papers.title: LogPpred: An AI-Based Predictive Model for Accurate Estimation of Molecular LogP.
papers.abstract: Lipophilicity, commonly described by the n-octanol/water partition coefficient (LogP), is a key physicochemical property influencing the pharmacokinetic behavior of small molecules. Reliable LogP estimation during the early stages of drug discovery is essential to support molecular design and prioritize compounds with favorable ADMET properties. In this work, we report the development of LogPpred, an AI-based predictor of molecular lipophilicity. Starting from a curated dataset of 13,536 molecules with experimentally determined LogP values, multiple machine learning algorithms and molecular re
papers.summary: LogPpred is a new AI-based model that predicts molecular lipophilicity (LogP) from a curated dataset of 13,536 experimental values, using machine learning to support early drug discovery. It provides accurate LogP estimates to help prioritize compounds with favorable ADMET properties.

papers.title: Effects of Co-Cultivation on the Phenolic Composition and Bioactive Properties of Basidiomycete Mycelia: Antioxidant, Photoprotective, Anti-Tyrosinase, and In Silico Evidence.
papers.abstract: Basidiomycetes produce a wide range of bioactive metabolites, yet the effects of fungal co-cultivation on phenolic composition and associated biological properties remain poorly understood. This study investigated the phenolic composition and antioxidant, photoprotective, and anti-tyrosinase activities of mycelial extracts obtained from four basidiomycetes cultivated either alone or in paired cultures. Phenolic compounds were characterized by HPLC, and the identified metabolites were further evaluated using target prediction, enrichment analyses, PASS prediction, ADME profiling, and toxicity a
papers.summary: This study explores how co-cultivating different basidiomycete fungi affects the phenolic composition and bioactive properties of their mycelial extracts, including antioxidant, photoprotective, and anti-tyrosinase activities. Using HPLC and in silico analyses, the authors identify changes in metabolite profiles and predict potential biological targets and safety, suggesting that fungal co-culture can modulate the production of beneficial compounds.

papers.title: Linear Residual Network Modeling for Anti-HIV-1 Activity Prediction and Docking-Validated Design of Biphenyl-DAPY-Based NNRTIs.
papers.abstract: To predict the anti-HIV-1 activity of biphenyl-DAPY-based non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs), a quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) analysis was conducted. Using the heuristic method (HM) for descriptor selection, four predictive models were established: support vector regression (SVR), kernel ridge regression, linear mixed-kernel SVR, and Linear Residual Network (LRNet). Rigorous validations, including leave-one-out cross-validation, fivefold cross-validation, and Y-randomization tests, confirmed their reliability. The LRNet model exhibited the best perfo
papers.summary: This study develops QSAR models to predict anti-HIV-1 activity of biphenyl-DAPY-based NNRTIs, with a Linear Residual Network (LRNet) showing the best performance. The models were validated through cross-validation and Y-randomization, and docking studies were used to design new compounds with improved predicted activity.

papers.title: Modeling microbiome modulation of tumor metabolic networks to predict synergistic therapies.
papers.abstract: Differences in microbiome composition profoundly influence drug response, yet methods to model the metabolic impact of microbes on host cells and therapeutics remain limited. We present a microbiome-aware computational framework combining machine learning and genome-scale metabolic models to predict combination therapies for colorectal cancer (CRC) in the presence of Fusobacterium nucleatum (Fn) and other pathogenic, probiotic, and commensal microbes. The model learned predictive metabolic flux signatures from 6,514 drug combination profiles in CRC cell lines and predicted synergistic drug com
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational framework that integrates machine learning with genome-scale metabolic models to predict how the microbiome influences drug responses in colorectal cancer. The model, trained on thousands of drug combination profiles, identifies synergistic therapies that account for the presence of specific microbes like Fusobacterium nucleatum, offering a new approach to microbiome-aware cancer treatment design.

papers.title: Integrated computational and preclinical evaluation of drug repurposing candidates for KRAS-mutant non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: KRAS mutations, particularly KRAS G12C, pose significant therapeutic challenges in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) due to limited inhibitor efficacy and rapid resistance. Drug repurposing offers a time and cost-effective strategy to identify alternative therapeutic options targeting KRAS-driven signalling. A structure-based drug repurposing approach was employed to screen FDA-approved compounds targeting key regulators to the MAPK signalling pathway and computationally modelled for potential engagement with the KRAS G12C switch-II pocket. Computational analyses including virtual screening,
papers.summary: This study uses a structure-based computational approach to screen FDA-approved drugs for repurposing against KRAS-mutant non-small cell lung cancer, focusing on compounds that may bind the KRAS G12C switch-II pocket. The authors identify promising drug candidates through virtual screening and computational modeling, which are then evaluated in preclinical models to assess their potential efficacy.

papers.title: Discovery of a potent TDP1 inhibitor through machine learning-driven predictive modeling combined with structure-based virtual screening and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Tyrosyl-DNA phosphodiesterase I (TDP1) repairs topoisomerase I (TOP1)-mediated DNA damage and is a promising anticancer target, particularly in combination with TOP1 inhibitors. However, the discovery of potent and drug-like TDP1 inhibitors remains challenging due to the limited structural diversity of known active compounds. Here, we developed an integrated computational framework combining machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and structure-based docking with experimental validation. A curated dataset of 2040 compounds (857 active, 1183 inactive) was assembled and analyzed by scaffold c
papers.summary: This study presents an integrated computational pipeline combining machine learning, deep learning, and structure-based virtual screening to identify novel TDP1 inhibitors, an anticancer target. The approach successfully discovered a potent compound with experimental validation, addressing the limited structural diversity of known TDP1 inhibitors.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence empowers targeted protein degradation: Core technological innovations, multi-scenario applications, and translational prospects.
papers.abstract: Targeted protein degradation (TPD) has emerged as a transformative therapeutic strategy that offers unprecedented opportunities to eliminate traditionally "undruggable" proteins that have posed significant challenges in traditional drug development. Current TPD approaches, including proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs), molecular glues, and lysosome-targeting chimeras (LYTACs), encounter several limitations. These include the complexity of forming stable ternary complexes, suboptimal design of linkers, a limited repertoire of E3 ligases, and inadequate pharmacokinetic properties. Artificia
papers.summary: This review discusses how artificial intelligence (AI) is being applied to overcome key challenges in targeted protein degradation (TPD), such as designing stable ternary complexes, optimizing linkers, and expanding the E3 ligase repertoire. It highlights AI's role in multi-scenario applications and translational prospects for therapies like PROTACs, molecular glues, and LYTACs.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Assisted Discovery of Chiral Azobenzene Dopants for Liquid Crystals.
papers.abstract: Cholesteric liquid crystals possess unique properties, such as selective reflection and circular polarization, due to their helical structures. The helical structures are determined by the helical twisting power (HTP) of chiral dopants. Chiral azobenzene compounds can change their HTP through photoisomerization, enabling photoresponsive tuning of the helical structure. For device applications, a large change in HTP value (ΔHTP) is desirable. In this study, we report a screening workflow to generate and identify chiral azobenzene compounds with high ΔHTP using machine learning (ML) and molecula
papers.summary: This study presents a machine learning-assisted screening workflow to identify chiral azobenzene dopants for liquid crystals that exhibit large changes in helical twisting power (ΔHTP) upon photoisomerization. By combining molecular generation and ML prediction, the authors efficiently discovered candidate compounds with high ΔHTP, which is desirable for photoresponsive device applications.

papers.title: Identification of novel PKR inhibitory chemotypes via integrated molecular modelling and machine learning.
papers.abstract: Interferon-inducible RNA-dependent protein kinase (PKR) is an emerging therapeutic target involved in cancer, neurodegeneration, and inflammatory disorders; however, the discovery of potent and structurally diverse PKR inhibitors remains limited. In this study, we report an integrated computational-experimental strategy for the identification of novel PKR inhibitory chemotypes. Pharmacophore models were generated from flexible docking of structurally diverse reference inhibitors and validated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. To better capture ligand flexibility and addre
papers.summary: This study presents an integrated computational-experimental approach to identify novel inhibitors of PKR, a therapeutic target in cancer and inflammatory diseases. By combining pharmacophore modeling, flexible docking, and machine learning, the authors discovered new chemotypes with PKR inhibitory activity, expanding the limited chemical diversity of known PKR inhibitors.

papers.title: Reliability of AI Methods in Drug Discovery: Evaluation of Boltz-2 for Structure and Binding Affinity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Despite continuing hype about the role of AI in drug discovery, no "AI-discovered drugs" have so far received regulatory approval. Here we assess one of the latest AI-based tools in this domain. Boltz-2, a recently developed biomolecular foundation model, aims to bridge the gap between AI efficiency and physics-based precision through a joint "cofolding" approach. In this study, we provide an extensive evaluation of Boltz-2 using two large-scale data sets: 16780 compounds for 3CLPro and 21702 compounds for TNKS2. We compare Boltz-2 predicted structures with traditional docking and binding affi
papers.journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation
papers.summary: This study evaluates Boltz-2, a recent AI-based biomolecular foundation model, for predicting protein structures and binding affinities in drug discovery. Using large-scale datasets for two targets (3CLPro and TNKS2), the authors compare Boltz-2's performance against traditional docking methods, finding that despite its promise, it does not yet achieve the accuracy needed for regulatory-grade drug discovery. The work highlights the current limitations of AI tools in this domain and underscores the need for further validation before AI-discovered drugs can reach approval.

papers.title: Design and synthesis of isoxazolidine core-based selective COX-2 inhibitors: in vitro inhibitor activity and in silico modeling.
papers.abstract: A novel series of tricyclic isoxazolidine-imidazole derivatives (3a-l) bearing diverse substituted phenyl groups were rationally designed, synthesized, and evaluated as selective cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) inhibitors. The target compounds were efficiently obtained via regio- and diastereoselective 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition of C-aryl-3-methylphenyl nitrones with 1-vinylimidazole. Comprehensive spectroscopic characterization was performed using FTIR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and LC-MS spectrometry. In vitro assays demonstrated potent COX-2 inhibition with minimal COX-1 activity, achieving high selectivity
papers.summary: This study reports the design and synthesis of novel isoxazolidine-imidazole derivatives as selective COX-2 inhibitors, which show potent COX-2 inhibition with minimal COX-1 activity in vitro. The compounds were synthesized via a regio- and diastereoselective cycloaddition and characterized by standard spectroscopic methods, with in silico modeling supporting their selectivity.

papers.title: STAT3 signaling inhibitors for cancer treatment.
papers.abstract: Pharmacological targeting of Signal Transducer and Activator of Transcription 3 (STAT3) in cancer has demonstrable antitumor efficacy. However, suitably potent, efficacious, and safe STAT3 inhibitors are scarce, and only a handful have entered clinical trials, limiting our knowledge of the extent of clinical benefit. Outcomes of recently completed trials in advanced cancers range from improved overall survival and complete responses in a cohort of patients with phosphotyrosine STAT3 positivity to partial responses and progressive disease in unselected patients. Advancements in oligonucleotide
papers.summary: This review discusses the current state of pharmacological targeting of STAT3 in cancer, highlighting that while antitumor efficacy has been demonstrated, only a few potent and safe inhibitors have reached clinical trials. Recent trial outcomes show improved survival in biomarker-selected patients but limited responses in unselected populations, and the authors point to advancements in oligonucleotide-based approaches as a promising direction.

papers.title: Discovery of Anti-Neuroinflammatory Compounds in Alzheimer's Disease: Current Trends and Future Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Chronic neuroinflammation in response to abnormal protein aggregates has been implicated as a critical mechanism in several neurodegenerative diseases, and the modulation of signaling pathways associated with inflammation is being explored as a potential strategy for new therapeutics. In Alzheimer's disease (AD), the neuroinflammation hypothesis also starts to influence the landscape of drug discovery in place of the previously regarded amyloid hypothesis. As such, the objective of this review is to compile recent advanced in the discovery of anti-neuroinflammatory compounds developed through
papers.summary: This review discusses the shift in Alzheimer's disease drug discovery from the amyloid hypothesis toward targeting neuroinflammation, highlighting recent advances in anti-neuroinflammatory compounds. It compiles current trends and future perspectives on modulating inflammatory signaling pathways as a therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: MOZAIC: Compound Growth via In Silico Reactions and Global Optimization using Conformational Space Annealing.
papers.abstract: Fragment-based drug discovery (FBDD) efficiently explores chemical space by combining small molecular fragments. Advances in computational methods are accelerating the development of algorithm- and AI-based approaches in FBDD. However, it should be noted that certain methods do not provide synthetic pathways to obtain the proposed compounds. Consequently, these molecules might not be synthesized easily.
papers.summary: MOZAIC is a computational tool for fragment-based drug discovery that grows molecular fragments into larger compounds using in silico reactions and global optimization via conformational space annealing. It addresses the limitation of many AI-based methods by ensuring that the proposed compounds have synthetic pathways, making them easier to synthesize.

papers.title: Integrated design, synthesis, biological evaluation, and computational mechanistic insights of novel benzanilide derivatives as VEGFR-2 targeted anticancer agents.
papers.abstract: VEGFR-2 is a key regulator of tumor angiogenesis and a validated target in anticancer drug discovery. In this study, a series of novel benzanilide derivatives (7a-7f and 9a-9b) were designed, synthesized, and evaluated as potential VEGFR-2 inhibitors. The design strategy was guided by key pharmacophoric requirements for VEGFR-2 inhibition. All compounds were synthesized successfully and characterized, then screened for in vitro cytotoxic activity against MCF-7, MDA-MB-231, HePG-2, and HCT-116 cancer cell lines, with WI-38 and WISH normal cells used for selectivity assessment. Among the tested
papers.summary: This study reports the design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of novel benzanilide derivatives as VEGFR-2 inhibitors for anticancer therapy. The compounds showed cytotoxic activity against multiple cancer cell lines with selectivity over normal cells, and computational studies provided mechanistic insights into their binding. This work contributes to the development of new VEGFR-2-targeted anticancer agents.

papers.title: Coumarin-based dual kinase inhibitors targeting CDK6 and VEGFR-2: experimental and computational validation.
papers.abstract: A rational pharmacophore-guided strategy was employed to design and synthesize a series of novel coumarin derivatives as potential dual cyclin-dependent kinase 6 (CDK6) and vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-2 (VEGFR-2) inhibitors. Following structural characterization, the synthesized compounds were evaluated for their anticancer activity against MCF-7, MDA-MB-231, HepG-2, and HCT-116 cancer cell lines, together with normal WI-38 and WISH cells. Among the tested derivatives, compound 7e exhibited the highest potency, with IC50 values ranging from 3.80 to 6.35 µM, while demonstrating
papers.summary: This study reports the design and synthesis of novel coumarin-based compounds as dual inhibitors of CDK6 and VEGFR-2, with compound 7e showing potent anticancer activity across multiple cancer cell lines. The work combines experimental evaluation with computational validation, offering a promising lead for dual-target cancer therapy.

papers.title: Heterocyclic chemistry meets wound care: novel p-methyl-m-trifluoromethyl-phenyl-substituted pyrrol-2-one derivatives with antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity.
papers.abstract: Biofilm-associated infections represent a major challenge in the treatment of antimicrobial-resistant pathogens, particularly in chronic and wound-related infections where bacterial adherence and persistence reduce therapeutic efficacy. To address this issue, we report a rapid, economical, and efficient one-pot three-component synthesis of 19 novel bis(trifluoromethyl)-dimethyl-substituted dihydro-pyrrol-2-one derivatives, providing a promising scaffold for the development of new antimicrobial and anti-biofilm agents. The structures of the synthesized compounds were confirmed by NMR, FT-IR, MA
papers.summary: This paper reports the synthesis of 19 novel pyrrol-2-one derivatives with antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity, targeting biofilm-associated infections common in chronic wounds. The compounds were produced via a rapid, economical one-pot three-component method and structurally confirmed by NMR, FT-IR, and mass analysis, offering a promising scaffold for new antimicrobial agents.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Antimicrobial Stewardship: From Clinical Decision Support to Public Health Action.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) continues to threaten the effectiveness of modern medicine and poses major public health challenges worldwide. Antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) programmes are essential to mitigate inappropriate antimicrobial use but are often resource-intensive and difficult to sustain. Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have generated interest in its potential to support stewardship activities across clinical, operational, and public health domains.
papers.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence can support antimicrobial stewardship programs, which are crucial for combating antimicrobial resistance but are often resource-intensive. It discusses AI applications across clinical decision support, operational efficiency, and public health surveillance, highlighting both opportunities and challenges.

papers.title: Machine learning-based prediction of SARS-CoV-2 bioactivity: integrating IC50 regression and activity classification using multi-task neural networks.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of compound bioactivity is essential for accelerating antiviral drug discovery and reducing experimental costs. Machine learning (ML) methods have shown considerable promise in modeling structure-activity relationships and compound potency. In this study, we present an integrated ML framework for predicting IC50 and pIC50 values of compounds active against SARS-CoV-2, key indicators of antiviral potency. The proposed framework comprises three complementary approaches: (i) a regression model for quantitative IC50 prediction validated against experimental data; (ii) a classif
papers.summary: This study presents a machine learning framework that integrates regression and classification models to predict the bioactivity (IC50/pIC50) of compounds against SARS-CoV-2, aiming to accelerate antiviral drug discovery. The multi-task neural network approach was validated against experimental data, demonstrating its potential to reduce experimental costs in early drug screening.

papers.title: AI-driven Identification of Zika Virus Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Research engaged with AI has dramatically increased due to a huge improvement of technologies in terms of cost and time-effectiveness as well as decreasing use of animals. High throughput screening (HTS) is a frequently used method in drug discovery. Here, we combined two powerful tools for AI-driven identification of Zika virus (ZIKV) inhibitors. The main complication from ZIKV is microcephaly and other related birth defects when pregnant women become infected with this virus. To date, there are no specific vaccines and antiviral drugs for the treatment of ZIKV infection. We have successfully
papers.journal: SLAS discovery : advancing life sciences R & D
papers.summary: This study combines two AI-driven tools with high-throughput screening to identify potential inhibitors of the Zika virus, which currently lacks specific vaccines or antiviral treatments. The approach aims to accelerate drug discovery by reducing cost, time, and animal use, addressing the urgent need for therapies against ZIKV, which causes severe birth defects.

papers.title: QSAR-Guided Virtual Screening and Molecular Dynamics Reveal Olaparib as a Repurposing Lead Against α-Synuclein Aggregation.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is characterised by the pathological aggregation of α-synuclein (α-syn) into Lewy body inclusions, yet no disease-modifying therapy exists. To address this, we developed an integrated computational pipeline combining quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modelling, structure-based virtual screening, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, and molecular mechanics Poisson-Boltzmann surface area (MM-PBSA) binding free energy calculations to repurpose FDA-approved drugs as α-syn fibril inhibitors. Two complementary QSAR model families were trained on 501 α-syn bi
papers.summary: This study presents a computational pipeline combining QSAR modeling, virtual screening, molecular dynamics, and MM-PBSA calculations to repurpose FDA-approved drugs as inhibitors of α-synuclein aggregation in Parkinson's disease. The approach identified olaparib as a promising lead compound that may bind to α-syn fibrils and prevent aggregation, offering a potential disease-modifying strategy.

papers.title: Molecular Docking and Simulation-Based Exploration of Niclosamide as a Potential Inhibitor of the p62 ZZ Domain.
papers.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) remains a therapeutic challenge due to complex oncogenic networks, including the often-undruggable MYC pathway. Here, we present an integrated in silico framework combining transcriptomic analysis, machine learning, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to explore potential therapeutic approaches targeting vault RNA1-1 (VTRNA1-1) in AML. RNA-seq profiling revealed that VTRNA1-1 depletion is associated with a profound disruption of the MYC and FOXM1 regulatory axes. To highlight compounds capable of recapitulating this transcriptomic signature, we developed a mach
papers.summary: This study uses an integrated computational approach combining transcriptomic analysis, machine learning, and molecular dynamics simulations to identify niclosamide as a potential inhibitor of the p62 ZZ domain, which may help target the MYC pathway in acute myeloid leukemia. The findings suggest a novel therapeutic strategy for AML by disrupting VTRNA1-1-associated oncogenic networks.

papers.title: Discovery of Novel AURKA Inhibitors for Triple-Negative Breast Cancer (TNBC) Therapy via a Hybrid Virtual Screening Pipeline, Biological Evaluation and Molecular Dynamics Simulation.
papers.abstract: Aurora kinase A (AURKA) is a pivotal driver of malignant progression and poor prognosis in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). In this study, we developed a cascaded AI-driven virtual screening pipeline, integrating sequence-based affinity prediction (PSICHIC), equivariant deep learning docking (KarmaDock), and geometric rescoring (DeepDock) to identify novel AURKA inhibitor candidates. From an in-house 160,000-compound screening library assembled from commercially available collections, three leads (compounds 3, 5, and 8) were selected and subsequently validated via HTRF biochemical assays,
papers.summary: This study presents a hybrid AI-driven virtual screening pipeline that combines sequence-based affinity prediction, deep learning docking, and geometric rescoring to identify novel AURKA inhibitors for triple-negative breast cancer. Three lead compounds were validated in biochemical assays, demonstrating the pipeline's effectiveness in discovering potential therapeutic candidates.

papers.title: Inhibition of amyloid β aggregation by venetoclax: a computational and in vitro experimental approach.
papers.abstract: The aggregation of amyloid β-protein (Aβ) plays a key role in the pathological progression of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Given the current absence of effective therapeutic strategies, the drug repurposing approach provides novel insights into the treatment of AD. Venetoclax, a B-cell lymphoma 2 (BCL-2) inhibitor, has demonstrated remarkable efficacy in the treatment of hematological malignancies, characterized by well-defined pharmacokinetic properties and a favorable safety profile. However, its effects and molecular mechanisms in the treatment of AD remain unexplored. Here, we investigated th
papers.summary: This study explores venetoclax, an existing cancer drug, as a potential treatment for Alzheimer's disease by computationally and experimentally testing its ability to inhibit amyloid beta aggregation. The findings suggest that venetoclax may reduce aggregation, offering a promising drug-repurposing avenue for AD therapy.

papers.title: Ziziphusine A, a unique plant-alkaloid featuring amide rotational isomerism from the fruits of Ziziphus jujuba with anti-inflammatory activity.
papers.abstract: Ziziphus jujuba var. inermis Rehder (Rhamnaceae) is an edible medicinal plant widely used in traditional medicine and functional foods. Phytochemical investigation of the methanolic extract of its fruits resulted in the isolation of a rare amide rotational isomeric alkaloid, ziziphusine A (1), together with eight known compounds including brassicasterol (2), (E)-24-nor-cholest-22-en-3β-ol (3), alphitolic acid (4), 3-O-cis-p-coumaroyl alphitolic acid (5), 3-O-trans-p-coumaroyl alphitolic acid (6), E-p-methoxycinnamic acid (7), (Z)-3-(4,5-dihydroxy-2-methoxyphenyl)acrylic acid (8), and scopoleti
papers.summary: This study reports the isolation of ziziphusine A, a rare alkaloid with amide rotational isomerism, from jujube fruits, along with eight known compounds. The compound and related isolates were evaluated for anti-inflammatory activity, highlighting the potential of jujube as a source of bioactive natural products.

papers.title: Design, preclinical evaluation, and multicenter phase 1 clinical study of HZ-A-018 for relapsed or refractory central nervous system lymphoma.
papers.abstract: Effective therapy for relapsed or refractory central nervous system lymphoma (r/r CNSL) remains an unmet medical need. Meanwhile, developing antitumor drugs for CNS malignancies faces the dual challenge of achieving effective blood‒brain barrier (BBB) penetration and potent tumor cell killing. To address these challenges, a comprehensive predictive system was established to support decision-making during the discovery of HZ-A-018, a potent and BBB-permeable Bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitor. This study further presents key preclinical results for HZ-A-018, as well as efficacy/safety data
papers.summary: This study describes the design, preclinical evaluation, and phase 1 clinical trial of HZ-A-018, a novel blood-brain barrier-permeable BTK inhibitor for relapsed/refractory central nervous system lymphoma. The drug showed promising efficacy and safety in early clinical testing, addressing a critical unmet need for CNS lymphoma therapy.

papers.title: An Interpretable Multi-Objective Machine Learning Framework for In Silico Prioritization of Anti-Staphylococcus aureus Antimicrobial Peptides.
papers.abstract: Background: Staphylococcus aureus, including methicillin-resistant lineages, is a leading cause of device- and catheter-related infection, and rising resistance motivates the search for antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) with strong anti-staphylococcal activity and low host toxicity. Machine learning can prioritize candidate peptides. However, the literature-derived AMP datasets are prone to homology-driven optimism, and computational studies frequently overstate their translational reach. Methods: We curated 4007 deduplicated S. aureus-active AMP records and 582 binary-labeled hemolysis records. E
papers.summary: This study presents an interpretable multi-objective machine learning framework to prioritize antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) with anti-Staphylococcus aureus activity and low hemolytic toxicity, addressing homology-driven bias in existing datasets. The authors curated a large, deduplicated dataset and built a model that balances activity and safety, providing a more realistic tool for in silico AMP screening.

papers.title: Recent advancements in artificial intelligence applications for the mitigation of antimicrobial resistance: challenges and opportunities.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a significant global public health threat, and efforts to mitigate it have been aided by artificial intelligence (AI) methods. Key areas of applications include rapid diagnostics, drug discovery and repurposing, surveillance and predictive modelling, and antibiotic stewardship. This review aims to summarize key literature on AI applications for mitigating AMR including original research articles from PubMed and Scopus published from October 2024 to 2025 to summarize and find out the way ahead for successful application of AI. The key search terms included w
papers.summary: This review summarizes recent AI applications for mitigating antimicrobial resistance (AMR), covering rapid diagnostics, drug discovery and repurposing, surveillance, predictive modeling, and antibiotic stewardship. It highlights key advances and challenges from literature published between October 2024 and 2025, and outlines future directions for successful AI integration in AMR mitigation.

papers.title: Geometric Deep Learning-Based Drug Design Models for Small-Molecule Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Deep neural network (DNN)-based in silico models show great promise in predicting the properties and bioactivities of novel compounds, including small molecules. Among traditional approaches, structure-based drug design (SBDD) remains a fundamental approach for drug discovery using molecular docking, scoring functions, and molecular dynamics simulations. However, these approaches are often constrained by limited flexibility, resolution, and generalizability. Geometric deep learning (GDL) offers a transformative alternative by enabling models to learn directly from non-Euclidean molecular repre
papers.summary: This review discusses how geometric deep learning (GDL) models are transforming small-molecule drug discovery by learning directly from non-Euclidean molecular representations, overcoming limitations of traditional structure-based drug design methods. It highlights GDL's potential to improve property prediction and bioactivity assessment for novel compounds.

papers.title: Identification and characterization of umami peptides from fermented soybean meal hydrolysates: Combined machine learning, cellular functional characterization, and structural interpretation.
papers.abstract: This study developed an efficient strategy for identifying umami and umami-enhancing peptides from fermented soybean meal hydrolysates (FSMH) to support the high-value utilization of soybean byproducts. An integrated approach combining virtual screening, molecular docking, sensory validation, intracellular calcium mobilization assays, and molecular dynamics simulation was employed. Sixteen peptides were synthesized for sensory validation, confirming 15 umami peptides. LE, AE, GEDLMVQ, and FEEINKV exhibited the strongest enhancement in both monosodium glutamate and inosinate/disodium guanylate
papers.summary: This study developed an integrated strategy combining machine learning, virtual screening, molecular docking, and cellular assays to identify umami and umami-enhancing peptides from fermented soybean meal hydrolysates. Fifteen peptides were confirmed as umami peptides, with LE, AE, GEDLMVQ, and FEEINKV showing the strongest enhancement effects, providing a method for high-value utilization of soybean byproducts.

papers.title: Efficient One-Pot Synthesis of Dibenzoxanthenes Using a Vinylimidazolium-Based Brønsted Acidic Ionic Liquid [VSBIM][Cl]: In Silico Evaluation of Drug-Likeness, ADMET Properties, PASS Analysis, Antiviral Activity Prediction, and Molecular Docking Studies.
papers.abstract: Dibenzoxanthene derivatives have produced considerable interest due to their pharmacological, photophysical, and organic optoelectronic properties. Herein, a facile one-pot methodology was developed for the synthesis of 14-(aryl)-14H-dibenzo[a,j]xanthene derivatives employing 5 mol% of the Brønsted acidic ionic liquid 1-vinyl-3-(4-sulfobutyl) imidazolium chloride [VSBIM][Cl] as an efficient and recyclable catalyst under solvent-free conditions. This protocol enables the condensation of β-naphthol with varied aryl or heteroaryl aldehydes to afford dibenzoxanthenes under neat conditions at 110°C
papers.summary: This paper presents a new one-pot synthesis method for dibenzoxanthene derivatives using a recyclable Brønsted acidic ionic liquid catalyst under solvent-free conditions. The authors also performed computational analyses (drug-likeness, ADMET, PASS, antiviral activity prediction, and molecular docking) to evaluate the potential pharmaceutical applications of the synthesized compounds.

papers.title: Computational investigation for exploring botanical ingredients as potential negative allosteric modulators targeting metabotropic glutamate receptor 5.
papers.abstract: Metabotropic glutamate receptors are class C G-protein-coupled receptors that respond to the neurotransmitter glutamate. In particular, metabotropic glutamate receptor 5 (mGluR5) has been a valuable drug target for the management of psychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders such as fragile X syndrome, autism, depression, anxiety, addiction, and movement disorders through negative allosteric modulators (NAMs). Despite the discovery of several NAMs, limited clinical efficacy was observed, thus preventing them from reaching the clinical stage. Natural products are indispensable, with a plethora
papers.summary: This study computationally screens botanical ingredients as potential negative allosteric modulators (NAMs) of metabotropic glutamate receptor 5 (mGluR5), a drug target for psychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders. The findings identify promising natural compounds that may serve as leads for developing more effective mGluR5 NAMs with better clinical efficacy.

papers.title: In silico discovery of CETP inhibitors from ZINC15 compounds using docking, ADMET filtering, and molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: Cholesteryl ester transfer protein is a crucial regulator of lipid metabolism and is considered a promising target for treating atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Given the clinical limitations and adverse effects of previous cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibitors, such as torcetrapib, this study aimed to identify safer, more effective alternatives through computational drug discovery.
papers.summary: This study used computational methods to identify potential new inhibitors of cholesteryl ester transfer protein (CETP), a key target for treating cardiovascular disease. By screening the ZINC15 compound database with docking, ADMET filtering, and molecular dynamics simulations, the authors discovered several promising candidates that may be safer and more effective than previous CETP inhibitors like torcetrapib.

papers.title: Antibacterial Activity of α-Sulfamidophosphonate Derivatives and Their In Silico Assessment as Dihydropteroate Synthase Binders.
papers.abstract: In this study, we report the first antibacterial evaluation of a focused library of 12 previously synthesized α-sulfamidophosphonate derivatives (4a-4l) against a panel of nine Gram-positive and Gram-negative strains, including ESBL- and carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales. The overall hit rate was modest, as most compounds were inactive at the highest tested concentration (MIC ≥ 256 µg/mL), indicating a narrow and strain-selective profile. Nevertheless, selected derivatives showed noteworthy activity against individual isolates: 4 g inhibited Staphylococcus aureus ATCC29213 at 4 µg/mL, 4
papers.summary: This study reports the first antibacterial evaluation of 12 α-sulfamidophosphonate derivatives against a panel of Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, including drug-resistant strains. Most compounds showed weak activity, but one derivative (4g) exhibited notable inhibition of Staphylococcus aureus at 4 µg/mL, and in silico docking suggested potential binding to dihydropteroate synthase.

papers.title: Machine learning approaches for electrocatalyst design in water splitting: a review for green hydrogen production.
papers.abstract: The production of green hydrogen through water splitting requires highly efficient electrocatalysts, but the current trial-and-error-based synthesis or discovery is time-consuming, costly and resource-intensive. Machine learning (ML) provides a powerful, data-driven alternative that can model complex structure-activity relationships across large chemical spaces at orders-of-magnitude speed. This review systematically overviews the life cycle of the electrocatalyst research and development application of ML. First, the thermodynamic and kinetic principles of the hydrogen and oxygen evolution re
papers.summary: This review discusses how machine learning can accelerate the discovery and design of electrocatalysts for green hydrogen production via water splitting, replacing slow trial-and-error methods. It systematically covers the ML workflow applied to electrocatalyst R&D, from data generation to model building, and highlights its potential to model complex structure-activity relationships rapidly.

papers.title: Advances in anti-aging Drug research leveraging multi-omics and artificial intelligence.
papers.abstract: The intensifying global population aging has rendered the development of anti-aging drugs a core challenge in the life sciences domain. Traditional models struggle to address the systemic and networked nature of aging. Multi-omics technologies provide a panoramic perspective for deciphering molecular networks of aging, while Artificial Intelligence (AI) has demonstrated significant advantages in target discovery, drug screening, and clinical trial optimization. This review systematically elaborates on the pathological characteristics and molecular mechanisms of aging, analyzes the application
papers.summary: This review discusses how multi-omics and artificial intelligence are being combined to advance anti-aging drug research, addressing the limitations of traditional models in capturing the systemic nature of aging. It highlights AI's role in target discovery, drug screening, and clinical trial optimization, offering a comprehensive overview of current strategies and future directions.

papers.title: A novel continuous-progression CKM model combined with multi-omics data integration identifies lipid metabolic drivers of disease progression.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome represents an emerging systemic disorder characterized by intertwined metabolic dysfunction, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular injury, yet robust preclinical models and mechanistic insights remain limited.
papers.summary: This paper introduces a novel continuous-progression CKM (cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic) model that integrates multi-omics data to identify lipid metabolic drivers of disease progression. The model provides a new preclinical framework for studying CKM syndrome and highlights specific lipid-related pathways that may drive the systemic disorder.

papers.title: CLEC7A as a potential biomarker of atherosclerotic response to aspirin therapy: a multi-omics analysis.
papers.abstract: Many patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) do not respond well to aspirin therapy. This study employed a multi-omics approach to identify key genes associated with aspirin non-responsiveness, thereby providing potential molecular targets and theoretical basis for improving the precision treatment strategies for ASCVD patients. One aspirin non-responsiveness dataset and two atherosclerosis-related datasets were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus database. After identifying differentially expressed genes through weighted gene co-expression network analysis and diffe
papers.summary: This study uses a multi-omics approach to identify CLEC7A as a potential biomarker for aspirin non-responsiveness in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease patients. The findings may help improve precision treatment strategies by providing molecular targets for patients who do not respond well to aspirin therapy.

papers.title: Drug sensitivity prediction across cancer types using graph isomorphism networks and biological pathway features: A dual-branch deep learning approach.
papers.abstract: Drug sensitivity prediction is an important issue within the precision medicine field. IC50, which is the molar drug dose needed to decrease the viability of cells by half compared to the drug-free control, is the main pharmacodynamics parameter used for drug sensitivity analysis in large-scale pharmacogenomics screenings. Computational estimation of IC50s based on molecular and genomic factors significantly reduces costs associated with experiments for measuring cell viability and allows for accelerating the process of drug discovery. Traditional methods of IC50 calculation do not allow integ
papers.summary: This paper presents a dual-branch deep learning model that combines graph isomorphism networks with biological pathway features to predict drug sensitivity (IC50) across cancer types. The approach improves prediction accuracy by integrating molecular and pathway-level information, offering a cost-effective computational alternative to experimental drug sensitivity assays.

papers.title: A call for principle-based acceptance of synthetic patients: establishing the AI-driven foundation for regulatory submissions.
papers.abstract: The pharmaceutical industry stands at the precipice of an AI-driven data revolution, with synthetic patients emerging as a transformative tool to accelerate drug discovery and development while enhancing patient privacy. However, a critical regulatory gap persists: the absence of a standardized basis from leading regulatory bodies for accepting AI-generated patient populations as evidence in regulatory submissions. This manuscript addresses this void by proposing five foundational principles-Representativeness, Utility, Robustness, Privacy Preservation, and Transparency-anchored by the "Fit fo
papers.summary: This paper proposes five foundational principles—Representativeness, Utility, Robustness, Privacy Preservation, and Transparency—to guide regulatory acceptance of AI-generated synthetic patients in drug development. It addresses the current lack of standardized regulatory frameworks for using synthetic patient data in submissions, aiming to accelerate drug discovery while protecting patient privacy.

papers.title: In silico drug discovery pipelines targeting antibiotic resistance: from genomes to leads.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is currently one of the leading global health threats. The evolution of drug-resistant bacterial pathogens is rapid, and there is a growing number of bacterial pathogens that have developed resistance to multiple antibiotics, and the rate at which new antibiotics are being developed is lagging far behind these two issues. In addition, historical drug discovery processes rely on conducting traditional in vitro-based studies to determine new antibiotics to use in practice. However, this process is becoming increasingly constricted due to high costs of conducting tr
papers.summary: This review discusses computational (in silico) drug discovery pipelines as a faster, cheaper alternative to traditional in vitro methods for identifying new antibiotics against resistant bacteria. It outlines how genomic data and bioinformatics tools can be used to move from bacterial genomes to lead compounds, addressing the urgent need for new antimicrobials.

papers.title: Clinical AI-assisted FXR prioritization and WADDAICA-guided design of a berberine-inspired analogue for MASH: integrated computational and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), lack effective targeted therapies despite increasing global prevalence. The farnesoid X receptor (FXR) is a key regulator of hepatic lipid metabolism, inflammation, and fibrosis, making it a promising therapeutic target. However, existing FXR modulators are associated with limited efficacy and adverse effects.
papers.summary: This study uses clinical AI-assisted prioritization of the FXR target and a computational method called WADDAICA to design a berberine-inspired analogue for MASH, with integrated computational and experimental validation. The work addresses the lack of effective targeted therapies for MASLD/MASH by developing a novel FXR modulator with potentially improved efficacy and safety.

papers.title: From benchmark accuracy to pharmacological credibility: why mechanistic explainability must define the next generation of AI for drug repurposing.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in drug repurposing to integrate chemical, biological, and clinical data and to prioritize candidate drug-disease associations. Yet current evaluation practices remain dominated by benchmark metrics such as AUROC, AUPRC, F1, or top- k  retrieval, which do not by themselves establish pharmacological credibility. A useful prediction is not merely one that scores highly on retrospective datasets, but one that can be connected to a biologically plausible mechanism, safety-relevant context, and a traceable evidentiary basis for experimental follow-u
papers.summary: This perspective argues that current AI models for drug repurposing are over-reliant on benchmark metrics like AUROC and F1, which fail to ensure pharmacological credibility. The authors advocate for a shift toward mechanistic explainability, where predictions are linked to biologically plausible mechanisms and traceable evidence to support experimental validation.

papers.title: From structural insight to molecule: Integrative molecular simulations identify candidate pyruvate kinase activators.
papers.abstract: Pyruvate kinase (PKLR) is a key glycolytic enzyme that regulates red blood cell energy homeostasis. Although Mitapivat is the first approved allosteric activator for pyruvate kinase deficiency (PKD), its clinical utility is limited by metabolic and pharmacokinetic challenges, underscoring the need for improved analogues. This study aimed to identify novel Mitapivat-derived scaffolds with enhanced PKLR binding, stability, and drug-like properties using an integrated computational approach. A total of 190 structurally related derivatives were screened through molecular docking, pharmacophore mod
papers.summary: This study uses an integrated computational approach, including molecular docking and pharmacophore modeling, to screen 190 Mitapivat-derived compounds as potential pyruvate kinase (PKLR) activators. The goal is to identify novel scaffolds with improved binding, stability, and drug-like properties to overcome the limitations of the current approved drug for pyruvate kinase deficiency.

papers.title: Bioinformatics identification of mitochondrial dynamics-related potential biomarkers in kawasaki disease and prediction of potential regulatory correlations.
papers.abstract: Kawasaki disease (KD) is a systemic vasculitis. Mitochondria was found to promote the activation of NLRP3 inflammatory vesicles, which have been shown to be a key driver of vascular disease. And there are few relevant reports of mitochondrial dynamic (MD) in KD. This study aimed to distinguish the potential biomarkers related to MD in KD and supply ideas for the intervention and treatment of KD. Currently, functional experimental verification in this field is lacking, and this study preliminarily explores their potential correlations through bioinformatics analysis.
papers.summary: This study uses bioinformatics to identify mitochondrial dynamics-related biomarkers in Kawasaki disease and predict their regulatory correlations. It provides preliminary insights into potential diagnostic markers and therapeutic targets for KD, though functional experimental validation is still lacking.

papers.title: Mechanistic insights into daidzin from Glycine max against breast cancer via network pharmacology and multi-level molecular modeling.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality in women, with around 2.3 million new cases and 670,000 deaths worldwide in 2022. Daidzin, a soy isoflavone glycoside from Glycine max, is a candidate bioactive scaffold, but its breast cancer-relevant mechanisms remain poorly defined. This study used an integrated in silico strategy combining network pharmacology and molecular modeling to prioritize daidzin targets and validate key interactions, with sirtinol as a reference compound. Target prediction identified 101 putative daidzin targets, and intersection with breast cancer-ass
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology and molecular modeling to investigate how daidzin, a soy isoflavone, may act against breast cancer. The authors identified 101 putative daidzin targets and validated key interactions, providing mechanistic insights into its potential anti-cancer effects.

papers.title: Functional restoration of conformational (R175H) and contact (R273H) mutant p53 by Bacillus-derived Hydroxymycotrienin A in non-small cell lung cancer: a computational approach.
papers.abstract: The TP53 mutations in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) remain a formidable clinical challenge. Current strategies, using the covalent binder APR-246, are limited by off-target toxicity and resistance.
papers.summary: This study computationally evaluates a Bacillus-derived compound, Hydroxymycotrienin A, as a potential therapeutic agent to restore function of two common mutant p53 proteins (R175H and R273H) in non-small cell lung cancer. The findings suggest this compound may bind and stabilize the mutant p53, offering a potential alternative to the existing drug APR-246, which has toxicity and resistance issues.

papers.title: Uncovering the molecular landscape of young-onset diffuse gastric cancer: A relieff-based feature selection analysis on RNA-Seq data.
papers.abstract: Diffuse Gastric Cancer (DGC) is an aggressive subtype with a poor prognosis and a lack of specific biomarkers, representing a critical unmet need in oncology. This study aimed to elucidate the key molecular drivers of DGC by integrating RNA-seq data with a multi-faceted bioinformatics approach.
papers.summary: This study uses RNA-seq data and a ReliefF-based feature selection method to identify key molecular drivers of young-onset diffuse gastric cancer (DGC), a particularly aggressive subtype with poor prognosis. The analysis reveals potential biomarkers and pathways that could aid in understanding the disease and developing targeted therapies.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses identify TRIP6 as a prognostic and EMT-associated biomarker in colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is characterized by profound molecular heterogeneity and complex tumor-microenvironment interactions, which contribute to invasion, metastasis, and variable clinical outcomes. More effective prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets are still needed.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to identify TRIP6 as a potential prognostic biomarker associated with epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in colorectal cancer. The findings suggest TRIP6 may serve as a therapeutic target and improve patient stratification.

papers.title: Bazedoxifene and Beyond: Identifying This SERM's Targets and Deciphering Its Molecular Mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Bazedoxifene (BZA), a third-generation selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) approved for osteoporosis treatment, is attracting attention for drug repurposing, especially in cancer research. While designed primarily for estrogen receptors, BZA exhibits in vitro off-target interactions that may explain novel therapeutic benefits or account for potential side effects. This review comprehensively examines both established and newly identified targets of BZA beyond estrogen receptors. To gather relevant data, we reviewed over 1500 articles selecting key studies proposing insights into BZA t
papers.journal: Advances in pharmacological and pharmaceutical sciences
papers.summary: This review catalogs the known and newly identified molecular targets of the drug bazedoxifene (BZA) beyond its primary estrogen receptor targets, drawing on over 1,500 articles. It highlights BZA's off-target interactions that may explain its potential for repurposing in cancer and other diseases, as well as possible side effects. The paper serves as a comprehensive resource for researchers exploring BZA's broader mechanisms of action.

papers.title: Network pharmacology and molecular modelling analysis of Arctium lappa phytochemicals in valproic acid-induced hepatotoxicity and pancreatitis.
papers.abstract: Valproic acid (VPA) is an antiepileptic drug commonly employed to treat epilepsy. Despite this, the clinical application of VPA is often hindered by adverse reactions. This study aims to investigate the therapeutic potential of phytochemicals obtained from Arctium lappa to mitigate VPA-induced toxicity and to determine the mechanisms involved.
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology and molecular modeling to investigate whether phytochemicals from Arctium lappa (greater burdock) can counteract the liver and pancreatic toxicity caused by the antiepileptic drug valproic acid. The analysis identifies key compounds and their potential protein targets, suggesting a mechanistic basis for their protective effects.
